budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said free cash is not yet fully certified but is looking relatively healthy, aided by a Lunenburg public schools turnback and higher investment income.
The prior capital plan was premised on a lower estimated free cash figure that will now be revisited once free cash is certified.

budget_items.topic: Fire Dept total FY27 budget request
budget_items.what_was_said: The chief presented the total fire/EMS budget request, noting a typo, and said it represents about a 22% increase driven mostly by the fourth shift proposal.
The chief said nearly all of the fire budget increase is the fourth shift except for a smaller remaining amount.
Radio maintenance is proposed to rise because portable radio costs have skyrocketed.
Vehicle maintenance is increasing; the chief cited an ambulance with major repair costs and ongoing truck issues.
A requested increase covers farming out vehicle repairs the highway garage can't perform.
The emergency management line, mostly supplies, is unchanged.
The department typically receives a state grant for fire safety and senior safety education.
A multi-year firefighter safety grant, believed ended, reappeared this year and is being spent down.
This federal-through-state grant has not materialized this year amid federal funding disruptions.
The department typically receives donated funds for equipment not covered by the town budget.
One-time mitigation funds are being used for added predium staffing in FY26 and paramedic training in FY27; the chief cautioned these are non-recurring.
The department currently budgets a set number of weekly predium hours, concentrated on Sundays.
Sunday shift predium coverage for three people was quantified in the Q&A on staffing.
A stipend line funds on-call officer coverage on Sundays; it would go away with full career staffing.
The utilities budget rises largely because the TCP building's utility costs are finally being captured in the budget.
The town is adjusting how solar credits are allocated across buildings after accumulating a large surplus that can't be directly applied elsewhere.
The facilities maintenance budget is presented as roughly level service with targeted increases for repairs and contracted maintenance.
A mandated 20-year sprinkler head inspection found failures at the fire department requiring replacement, below the capital threshold.
The town's betterment cost for sewer installation expires after FY28, freeing budget room afterward.
The parks budget rises mainly due to purchase-of-service costs for landscaping and repairs.
The current landscaping contract doesn't cover enough mowing cuts for baseball season and would need additional funding to meet the needed frequency.
The revolving fund collects rent from public access TV and the Shapiro school leasing classrooms, offsetting TCP building costs.

A prior-year capital appropriation for the TCP roof was found to be double-counted with FY26 capital funding for town hall windows/HVAC design; a cleanup warrant article will rescind the original vote.
The police budget is mostly personnel costs driven by the collective bargaining agreement, stipends, overtime and training.

Vehicle maintenance is level-funded based on recent years' actuals, aided by cycling in two new cruisers annually.
The lockup line dropped substantially after the town began sending most male prisoners to the Worcester County Sheriff instead of holding them locally.
A state grant funds a co-response mental health clinician shared with Lancaster, which had been lost and then restored.
The department was not awarded its usual highway traffic safety grant this year, which normally funds radar units.
Comfort dog handling fees are a separate cost per dog; an unused second comfort dog would add another handling fee if utilized.
The Town Manager said the preliminary FY27 budget as presented is not balanced and relies on an override of this size, which she expects to keep changing.
Property tax, state aid, local receipts and enterprise funds were broken out as shares of total FY27 revenue.
Enterprise fund revenue is still being finalized pending sewer and PACK enterprise indirect cost work.
The maximum allowable levy calculation starts from last year's levy limit plus the allowable Proposition 2½ increase.

transfers.description: A reserve fund transfer was needed last year to cover fire department vehicle maintenance overruns.

Prior-year capital appropriation intended for the TCP building roof will instead be redirected via a cleanup warrant article, after it was found to have been double-counted with FY26 capital plan funding for town hall window/HVAC design.

decisions.decision: Fire department will use Noba mitigation one-time funds for added predium (call staff) staffing in FY26 and set aside funds for paramedic training in FY27, rather than offsetting the fourth shift's ongoing cost.

A Finance Committee public hearing on the budget is currently slated for March 19th, though members flagged it may be too soon given other pending money articles.

minutes.headline: Town Manager unveiled a preliminary FY27 budget that does not balance without a property tax override
minutes.summary: The Finance Committee heard FY27 budget presentations from the fire, facilities and police departments, each citing staffing, contract and equipment cost drivers, including a fire department fourth-shift staffing proposal and a police restructuring from two school resource officers to one SRO plus a second detective. The Town Manager then presented a preliminary town-wide FY27 budget that she said does not balance and currently relies on a Proposition 2½ override, walking the committee through revenue sources and expenditure categories in detail; no votes were taken on the budget or the override. She also reported that FY25 books were closed out late, risking a hold on state aid, though the town secured a filing extension.

what_happened.line: The Town Manager presented a preliminary FY27 town budget that does not balance and currently relies on a Proposition 2½ override.
No votes were taken on the budget or the override; the presentation was informational only.
The fire department outlined a fourth-shift staffing proposal as its main FY27 cost driver.
Police described shifting from two school resource officers to one SRO plus a second detective, citing cyber crimes against children.
FY25 books closed late, risking a hold on state aid; the town secured a filing extension.

why_it_matters: An override, if it reaches a ballot, would raise property taxes beyond the state cap and needs voter approval.
The fire department's added shift and the police restructuring both affect staffing levels and response for residents.
A late FY25 closeout touches the town's cash flow and its standing for state aid, even though an extension was obtained.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records overlap heavily on the FY27 financial summary (revenue, levy, expenditure-by-category totals, deficit/override math) and agree there, once you allow for digit-grouping/decimal-point caption garbling on our side — dozens of figures are the same fact rendered badly. But the official minutes are themselves a curated summary: they omit almost every granular departmental line our transcript captured (radio maintenance, sprinkler, drainage, IT contractor, etc.), while we're missing the police compensation table, mutual-aid stats, and cruiser count the official minutes include; a reader should specifically check the TCP revolving-fund balance ($6,000–24,000 heard vs. $33,500 official), the police lockup line ($125,000 heard vs. $20,600 official), and whether the SRO-to-detective move and next week's meeting topic were actually decided as our minutes state.
